title: Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits of coherent formal modules
statement: Let X be Noetherian, I a quasi-coherent ideal and U an open subscheme with its Noetherian instance. The explicit full-subcategory termwise restriction functor defined by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-restriction-objects] preserves finite limits and finite colimits in Coh(X,I) and Coh(U,I|U), whose abelianness is [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. This is a preservation statement only; it asserts no local reflection of exactness.

proof.text: Use abelianness on X and U to supply finite products, equalizers, finite coproducts, coequalizers and zero objects. Transport the finite biproduct instance across the unique zero-morphism structures.

proof.text: The inclusion preserves cokernels by ambient cokernel closure. Right whiskering by ordinary restriction preserves colimits. The restricted inclusion composite is definitionally the original inclusion followed by right whiskering. Since the target inclusion is fully faithful it reflects colimits, so the formal restriction functor preserves cokernels.

proof.text: From the stabilized kernel construction obtain the zero-transition property of its levelwise kernel. Reuse formalMono_of_kernel_transition_zero from CoherentFormalModuleKernel (a proof-only import all exposes this private helper) to make the constructed arrow mono: an annihilated map vanishes after precomposition with each epi transition. Ordinary module restriction preserves kernels, so PreservesKernel.iso_inv_ι transports the zero-transition equations and proves the restricted constructed arrow mono. Build the global limiting fork using the existing factorization theorem; compare it with any given limiting fork and transport restricted monicity through the comparison isomorphism.

proof.text: For every fork over the restricted alpha, the new factorization-existence lemma supplies a lift. Restricted monicity proves uniqueness by cancellation. Fork.IsLimit.mk' builds the limiting restricted fork; KernelFork.isLimitMapConeEquiv yields preservation of kernels. Mathlib Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesCokernels complete both conclusions.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModules_restriction_limits {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (U : X.Opens)
    [IsNoetherian U.toScheme] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (coherentFormalModulesRestriction I U) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits (coherentFormalModulesRestriction I U)
